decisions: D2 (US-010, PRD §9 Q2): Auto always answers; a specialist never takes over the owner's chat with its own persona and tools; a message that names an agent or role files a ticket (ASSIGN) and Auto reports the number. The DELEGATE lane is removed from api/chat.py.

D3 (US-013, PRD §9 Q3): built only if the owner's four-arm run (US-009) records a median prep_ms above 2,000 ms; the loop reads the owner's note on US-009 before starting US-013 and marks US-013 `SKIPPED — prep_ms under 2 s` if the note says so, or `→ BLOCKED — no US-009 note yet` if there is no note. A SKIPPED or BLOCKED story never stops the wave: the PR opens and CI runs on the rest.
D4 (Jev, PRD §9 Q4): not in this PRD. Nothing goes live; the shadow keeps recording.

D5 (failover model, PRD §9 Q5): NONE. A provider refusal or rate limit fails the turn honestly (turn_errors), never a silent answer on another model; the config key `LLM_FAILOVER_MODEL` exists, defaults to empty, and is the only place a failover could be set.
D6 (the ATOM lane, PRD §9 Q6): kept, with the promoted tools shipped on it (Wave 1 US-006).
D9 (one PR per wave): as Wave 1: story commits end with ' [skip ci]', the draft PR is opened once by the runner when the build is COMPLETE, one CI run per wave.

D11 (stacking): until Wave 1 is on main, this branch is STACKED on feat/prd-256-w1-receipts-gates and starts as soon as Wave 1 is pushed for its CI (owner, 6 Oct: no waiting on the previous wave's CI). Never merge Wave 1 or main into this branch.
project: PRD-256 Auto, receipts not narration — Wave 2: the model, Auto always answers, one hand-off table, the families deleted
description: Wave 2 of PRD-256 (docs/PRDS/PRD-256-AUTO-RECEIPTS-GATES-CONTRACTS.md). US-008..US-013 in priority order: the Claude-ready LLM manager (sampling params, price table, an explicit failover); the four-arm run is the owner's (US-009, OWNER); Auto always answers and named agents get tickets (the DELEGATE lane removed); one hand-off table instead of four lanes; the regex claim families deleted once the receipts rule is proven; context assembly under two seconds, only if US-009's measurement says so. Stacked on Wave 1 until Wave 1 is on main. The decisions above are binding. Diff base for every check: `bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd256w2.sh --print-base`.
ownerTest: US-009 is the owner's run: the four arms (gemini-0.7, gemini-0.2, sonnet-5, haiku-4.5) on the eval set after Wave 1 is on main; the table in runs/results.md; the default model decision; write the median prep_ms per arm into the US-009 note (US-013 reads it).
US-010 in the browser: 'Give #<card> to <agent>' assigns the named card and makes no copy; an ask with no agent named is answered by Auto (agent-info says Auto).
Night 12 in c1 on a fresh build from main only once the eval passes its bars (PRD §10).
Both editions: the same checks on the local stack and, after deploy, on SaaS.

userStories.title: A Claude-ready LLM manager
userStories.description: As the operator, I want a Claude 4.6+ model to be a one-line switch for Auto, so the model test and the decision cost nothing in plumbing.
acceptanceCriteria: Sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, top_k) are omitted for Claude 4.6+ model ids on every client path (core/llm/clients/anthropic_client.py, the OpenRouter path through openai_compatible_client.py / openai_chat_request.py), through the existing per-model check in core/llm/clients/base.py (the OpenAI-reasoning-model rule extended, one function, no copy). → DONE — a76667e10: core/llm/clients/base.py's one rule (_REJECTS_SAMPLING / accepts_sampling_params) now covers Opus and Sonnet 4.6 too; the OpenRouter/NVIDIA/DeepSeek adapter's _base_kwargs builds through openai_chat_request.chat_kwargs with sampling=accepts_sampling_params(model) (it sent temperature on every call); anthropic_client.py already read the rule. Older Claude ids (Haiku 4.5) keep temperature and drop top_p beside it (takes_one_sampling_param, the 'not both' 400). Note: per Anthropic's docs Opus/Sonnet 4.6 still accept sampling; they are folded in so the whole 4.6+ family shares one request shape, as the criterion says.

core/llm/manager.py's price table gains claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-opus-5 at list price (input, output per 1k tokens), ordered longest-key-first as the table requires. → DONE — a76667e10: _MODEL_COST_ENTRIES gains claude-sonnet-5 (0.002, 0.010), claude-opus-5 (0.005, 0.025), claude-haiku-4-5 and OpenRouter's claude-haiku-4.5 (0.001, 0.005); MODEL_COST_MAP sorts longest-key-first, so Haiku 4.5 is no longer priced as claude-haiku-4. manager.py did not grow (1,043 lines, the two except branches folded into _call_failed/_raise_unavailable).

A config key `LLM_FAILOVER_MODEL` in orchestrator/config.py (default empty) named in reports/config-surface.json; with it empty, a rate-limited or refused provider call fails the turn honestly through turn_errors and never answers on another model; the receipts frame carries the model that answered. → DONE — a76667e10: config.LLM_FAILOVER_MODEL (default empty) in config.py and reports/config-surface.json; core/llm/failover.py reads it: empty, the manager re-raises the provider's typed refusal (turn_errors → rate_limited) and asks no other model; set, a refused call is asked once on it, never itself, and the reply's model is the one the receipts frame (receipts_frame/model_of, Wave 1) names.

Reasoning passthrough for Claude via OpenRouter is covered by a recorded-transport test (the request carries the reasoning setting the manager already uses; the response's reasoning deltas reach the existing PRD-238 stream). → DONE — a76667e10: test_claude_reasoning_through_openrouter_reaches_the_stream drives stream_response on a recorded transport: the request carries no reasoning field (the manager sets none; OpenRouter's default stands) and the recorded reasoning deltas reach on_delta('reasoning', …) and LLMResponse.reasoning (PRD-238).

Tests: `orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_llm_manager_claude5_params.py` with a recorded transport (no temperature on a Sonnet 5 request; the governor prices it; the failover comes from config and is empty by default). → DONE — a76667e10: orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_llm_manager_claude5_params.py (recorded transport: no temperature/top_p/top_k on a Sonnet 5 request, streaming and not; estimate_cost_usd prices the arms; LLM_FAILOVER_MODEL empty by default, a 429 fails the turn with one call; failover only from config); test_anthropic_sampling_params.py moved the 4.6 ids with the reason in its docstring.

ruff and the changed-line code-shape gate pass on the touched lines (functions ≤ 50 code lines, nesting ≤ 4, no file grown past 800 lines) → DONE — scripts/ci/check_changed_code_shape.py: 0 errors on changed code; py_compile clean; ruff is not on PATH here (CI runs it).
pushed; CI runs ONCE at the end of the wave on the draft PR the runner opens (never per story) → DONE — committed with [skip ci]; CI runs once at the end of the wave.

acceptanceCriteria: → OWNER: arms A to D on the eval pack after Wave 1 is on main; one table in runs/results.md with the four rates, cost per 100 asks, p50 turn latency and median prep_ms per arm; the bars: claims backed ≥ 95%, wrong-surface ≤ 5%, first-time-right ≥ 80%, owner-only without a click = 0.

userStories.title: Auto always answers; work goes to agents on tickets
userStories.description: As an owner, I want Auto to be the one voice in my chat, so a specialist never answers me in its own persona and the work goes to the team on tickets I can see.
acceptanceCriteria: The DELEGATE lane is removed from api/chat.py: `UniversalRouter` is no longer imported or called by the chat dispatch; no chat turn is answered by an agent other than Auto unless the owner chose that agent in the UI (request.agentId).

A message that names an agent or role resolves to the ASSIGN lane (apply_assign_bias): Auto files the ticket for that agent with the dispatch contract and reports the number; a role with no roster match asks once, as today.

The Tier-3 rubric in consumers/chatbot/auto.py drops 'delegate … (Most molecule/cell/organ work.)' and its example; `Action.DELEGATE` maps to RESPOND with the platform tools; the 24-hour verdict cache is bypassed for any verdict that would have routed away (the cache key or the store skips them).
The Jev shadow keeps recording the classifier unchanged; nothing reads its agreement as a quality signal.

Tests: `orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_auto_answers_unless_named.py` on the dispatch (an unnamed ask → Auto; 'Give #0192 to the Support Agent' → ASSIGN on the named card, no copy; a chosen agentId → that agent); the F263 and F241 tests updated with the reason in their docstrings.

acceptanceCriteria: Preconditions, read from the owner's US-009 note before starting: the post-wave-1 eval shows claims backed ≥ 95% on the chosen arm.
